description: Returns a list of asset types for a given project.

parameters.name: asset_type_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of Asset Type IDs to filter by

parameters.name: include_asset_counts
parameters.description: When true, each item includes assetCount for this type only, scoped to the project. Defaults to false when omitted.

parameters.name: eligible_sub_asset_of
parameters.description: Parent asset ID. When supplied, returns only the asset types eligible to receive sub-assets of that parent (a flat, eligibility-scoped list for the Link Sub-Assets dialog).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sorting criteria in minus-based order format. Default sort order is ascending. Multiple sort criteria can be provided in CSV format, for example: sort=name,-created_at. Default sorting is by displa...

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

parent_type_id.description: Deprecated: use 'parents'. Single parent type ID kept for backward compatibility; set to the lowest-display-order parent.

overridden.description: True when the Asset Type ID is overridden for this project. Project-scoped reads only.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.
